channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Employment – Lie detector – Online assessment
item.description: Where a plaintiff applied for a job with the defendant, which required the plaintiff to complete an online assessment called a “Virtual Job Tryout” (VJT), the plaintiff’s complaint under the Massachusetts lie detector statute must be dismissed because the facts alleged in his complaint do not plausibly suggest that the VJT was a lie detector test within the meaning of the statute.

item.title: Employment – Trade secrets
item.description: Where a plaintiff has alleged misappropriation of trade secrets and confidential information by two defendants who used to work for the plaintiff, the complaint should not be dismissed despite the defendants’ argument that the plaintiff has failed to identify with precision what information or knowledge the defendants took and why it qualifies for protection as trade secrets or confidential business information.

item.title: Contract – Marketing agreement
item.description: Where a plaintiff alleging breach of a marketing agreement has filed a motion for a preliminary injunction, that motion should be denied because the plaintiff has not met its burden of showing that any harm caused by the defendants’ alleged misconduct could not adequately be compensated with money damages.

item.title: Jurisdiction – Venue – BLS
item.description: Where a plaintiff who resides in Maryland has filed a fraud complaint against a defendant who resides in Holden, Worcester County is the proper venue, so the case should be transferred there.

item.title: Securities – Fraud
item.description: Where a complaint has been filed by a plaintiff who authorized his son to invest the plaintiff’s money in investment vehicles offered by the defendants, summary judgment should be denied because issues exist regarding whether the money used to purchase the securities, which came out of a joint account, was actually the plaintiff’s money and whether he was the actual purchaser of the securities.

item.title: Contract – Prompt Payment Act
item.description: Where a plaintiff has moved for summary judgment under the Prompt Payment Act, that motion should be allowed because the defendant general contractor did not properly refuse payment in writing in a timely manner.

item.title: Search and seizure – Exit order
item.description: Where a defendant has challenged the denial of his motion to suppress, arguing that a police officer lacked a lawful basis to order him to step out of his car, a remand must be ordered because it is unclear whether the lower court credited portions of the officer’s testimony that are critical to determining whether the exit order was reasonable.

item.title: Criminal – Lack of prosecution
item.description: Where a criminal complaint charging a defendant with possession of heroin with intent to distribute and possession of omeprazole was dismissed for lack of prosecution because the commonwealth “refused a court order to bring the alleged drugs in” for a hearing on a motion to suppress, the judge abused his discretion both by deeming the commonwealth’s conduct a failure to prosecute and by refusing the prosecutor's request for a continuance.

item.title: Prisons – Appellate entry fee – Waiver
item.description: Where (1) a Superior Court judge denied a plaintiff’s motion for extra fees and costs to hire an expert witness, (2) the plaintiff sought interlocutory relief from a single justice of the Appeals Court pursuant to G.L.c. 231, §118, and (3) the plaintiff moved for a waiver of the appellate entry fee, the single justice’s order requiring the payment of a partial entry fee must be reversed because the single justice erroneously relied upon G.L.c. 261, §29.

item.title: Search and seizure – Consent – Exit order
item.description: Where a defendant who was ordered out of his vehicle during a routine traffic stop filed a motion to suppress, that motion should have been allowed because (1) the exit order was unlawful and (2) the commonwealth has failed to carry its burden of demonstrating that the defendant's consent was sufficiently attenuated from the unlawful exit order to purge the taint of the constitutional violation.
